review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should provide meaningful information making stakeholders aware of interactions with AI, including workplace interactions.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Section 1.3(ii) is used as a nonbinding comparative benchmark for AI actors and the the May–July 2026 customer-routing/distillation campaigns, with evidenced model evaluation/traceability or customer AI interaction scope in 2026. No binding or certified conformity claim is made.
previous_canonical_assessment.finding_basis: The reported customers believed they were interacting with Kimi or DeepSeek AI services and received AI responses. That establishes awareness of AI interaction for this narrow OECD proposition. Silent substitution of Claude and undisclosed training are separate source/purpose issues; this benchmark does not require exact provider/model identity or authorize secondary use.

review.reason_for_change: Anthropic reports that Moonshot users believed they were using Kimi while receiving Claude responses. Those users understood the interaction as AI-mediated. The result covers awareness of interacting with AI. It does not validate the undisclosed backend identity or customer-data routing.

review.reason_for_change: The customer-query routing does not identify affective-data processing or an emulated-empathy partner system. Ordinary customer conversations and distillation do not establish those system types.

conclusion_change.previous: The reported conduct separates into three mechanisms. Customer requests were silently relayed from the selected service to Claude, changing the processing principal and creating an authority-scope boundary whose contractual or consent basis is not public. The customer-facing responses were also represented as coming from the selected service/model even though Anthropic reports Claude generated them, creating a source-attribution failure. Separately, saved exchanges and extracted reasoning traces were used for training/distillation, a materially different secondary purpose, and the campaign scale supports Industrial-Scale Capability Extraction. VIGIL preserves Anthropic's attribution as provider-reported evidence rather than an independent legal finding. Provider-attributed source misrepresentation and secondary-purpose/cumulative extraction failures remain distinct from unresolved cross-provider customer authority and consequential trust-cue effects. OECD AI awareness does not require identification of the exact model; users knew they interacted with an AI service, while provider substitution remains a separate taxonomy issue.
